claims.statement: AWARE I reports 2060 arrest events, 330 discharge survivors, 140 stage 1 and 101 stage 2 interviewees. Printed 52 plus 90 interviews and a Table 1 denominator of 142 conflict with 140; the discrepancy is unresolved.
alternative_explanations: Selection, recall timing and memory processes limit inference; no specific ordinary mechanism is established by this record.
limitations: No rawparticipantdata orfinal-versionreconciliation.

claims.statement: AWARE I classifies 9 of 101 stage 2 interviewees as NDE (Greyson score at least 7), including two event-recall cases; 46 non-NDE memories and 46 no-memory reports are different groups.
alternative_explanations: Selection, recall timing and memory processes limit inference; no specific ordinary mechanism is established by this record.
limitations: Conditional onsurvival/interview; notall-arrestprevalence.

claims.statement: Both AWARE I event-recall cases lacked installed shelves at their arrest locations. The main study abandoned programmed auditory cues after the pilot.
alternative_explanations: Selection, recall timing and memory processes limit inference; no specific ordinary mechanism is established by this record.
limitations: No concealed-targettest ofthese 2 reports; overall exposed-intervieweddenominatorunknown.

claims.statement: AWARE I authors report medical-record corroboration for one event-recall case and infer approximately three minutes from an AED sequence; no patient-specific neural recording establishes absent processing.
alternative_explanations: Selection, recall timing and memory processes limit inference; no specific ordinary mechanism is established by this record.
limitations: Project didnotinspect chart; timinginferred, notEEG-aligned;ordinaryinformationroutesnotexcluded.

claims.statement: The Dutch study reports 344 people, 509 successful resuscitation episodes, 62 broad NDE reports and 41 core NDE reports. People and episodes are different units.
alternative_explanations: Selection, recall timing and memory processes limit inference; no specific ordinary mechanism is established by this record.
limitations: Author-copyextractionprovisionaltoerratum; initialarrest/survivorattritionunknown.

claims.statement: Dutch year-two follow-up initially interviewed 37 previous NDE participants and 37 selected controls; reclassification yielded 35 NDE and 39 no-NDE participants. Year eight retained 23 and 15 respectively.
alternative_explanations: Selection, recall timing and memory processes limit inference; no specific ordinary mechanism is established by this record.
limitations: Samecohort; controlsselected from 75 contacted; notindependentreplication.

claims.statement: Dutch authors acknowledge possible site selection and use estimated arrest timing; no participant-specific EEG during reported experience is presented.
alternative_explanations: Selection, recall timing and memory processes limit inference; no specific ordinary mechanism is established by this record.
limitations: Absence ofreportedmeasurement doesnotestablishabsenceofprocessing; no mechanismidentified.

claims.statement: Martial and colleagues challenge AWARE II EEG classification and missing data, terminology, common-fruit interpretation, and exclusion of pre-arrest or recovery timing.
alternative_explanations: Selection, recall timing and memory processes limit inference; no specific ordinary mechanism is established by this record.
limitations: Criticism attribution; AWARE II main text now inspected, but the direct author reply remains inaccessible.

claims.statement: The teaching compilation contains only the AWARE II abstract and references. A later user-supplied full article provides the main text; these are access versions of one underlying article, not independent studies.
alternative_explanations: Selection, recall timing and memory processes limit inference; no specific ordinary mechanism is established by this record.
limitations: Access provenance statement only.

claims.statement: PubMed indexes an erratum to van Lommel 2001 at Lancet 2002;359(9313):1254; its contents were not accessed.
alternative_explanations: Selection, recall timing and memory processes limit inference; no specific ordinary mechanism is established by this record.
limitations: Unknown impact; no corrected-valueclaim.

claims.statement: AWARE II recruited 567 subjects: 213 sustained ROSC, 53 discharged, 28 interviewed, and 11 with memories/perceptions. Twenty-five discharge survivors were not interviewed.
limitations: Source reporting verified; underlying participant records were not independently audited.

claims.statement: AWARE II interview categories overlap: two CPR-related emergence, two post-resuscitation emergence, three dream-like, and six recalled experiences of death among 11 reporters. No external signs of consciousness were reported.
limitations: Source reporting verified; underlying participant records were not independently audited.

claims.statement: AWARE II reports combined tablet/headphones for 365 of 567 subjects. The main text does not identify the confirmed target-exposed/interviewed intersection.
limitations: Equipment deployment is not verified exposure at the scheduled stimulus time.

claims.statement: AWARE II reports no explicit image or auditory-stimulus recall among 28 interviewed survivors, no implicit visual identification, and one correct three-fruit choice in the implicit exercise.
source_locators: p7 Explicit recall and implicit learning
limitations: The one fruit choice is not explicit hearing; no valid opportunity rate or chance probability established.

claims.statement: AWARE II captured 851 EEG images from 85 subjects; 466 images from 53 subjects were interpretable, and 49 of those subjects also had rSO2.
limitations: Images and people are distinct denominators; artifact and equipment losses are material.

claims.statement: AWARE II Fig. 2 states that two of 28 interviewed subjects had EEG data, and neither was among those with explicit cognitive recall.
limitations: This wording does not establish absence of all experience or every possible physiological association; no content-specific timing is given.

claims.statement: AWARE II authors report near-normal/physiological EEG rhythms up to 35–60 minutes into CPR, using limited frontotemporal screenshots during pulse-check pauses; alpha-coma interpretation could not be excluded.
source_locators: pp3–4 recording; p4 Fig. 1; p9 Results/limitations
limitations: Aggregate physiology does not time a particular reported experience. Figure points/bins extend beyond the body timing summary; exact maximum unresolved.

claims.statement: AWARE II separately analyzes 126 selected community survivors with self-reported experiences. This ancillary qualitative arm is not an all-arrest prevalence sample.
source_locators: p2 cross-sectional methods; p6 Results; pp5,8 Table 2B/Fig. 3
limitations: Overlap with prospective participants or previous published narratives not established.

claims.statement: AWARE II authors report chart verification of one shock recollection, with no further information provided for independent corroboration; they also acknowledge unmeasured prior knowledge of resuscitation.
limitations: Project did not inspect charts. Correct event recall alone does not establish an anomalous information route or exact experience timing.

claims.statement: AWARE II notes that further analyses of these EEG/rSO2 datasets are presented in separate manuscripts; such analyses must be checked for shared participants before being counted as independent replications.
limitations: Specific companion publications and exact overlap counts were not inspected.

arguments.name: Conditional inference to brain independence
premises: Prospectively recruited survivors report lucid experiences; the AWARE studies report limited chart corroboration of resuscitation details.
bridge_principles: The reported experience must be independently timed to conditions excluding the neural processes required by a specified dependence model.
Ordinary information access and memory reconstruction require assessment; report accuracy alone does not supply the missing timing premise.
arguments.conclusion: These studies motivate discriminating tests but do not establish H-B in this packet.
arguments.strongest_objection: No concealed target success with established opportunity and no content-specific experience during measured absent processing are demonstrated.
arguments.strongest_reply: Incomplete measurements do not refute testimony or establish an ordinary explanation of each case.
unresolved_issues: Timing and substrate exclusion; target opportunity; irreversible death not studied.

arguments.name: Physiological and methodological countercase
arguments.position: Challenges inference to H-B without establishing physicalism
premises: AWARE II records some organized rhythms during CPR, with substantial missingness and limited montage.
Recall timing, prior knowledge, selection and ambiguous fruit-choice interpretation remain unresolved.
bridge_principles: A possible mechanism is not a demonstrated explanation of a particular account.
Aggregate EEG correlations cannot identify or causally explain an unlinked person’s reported contents.
arguments.conclusion: Brain-dependent possibilities remain open; neither physicalism nor brain independence is settled.
arguments.strongest_objection: Generic possibilities do not explain each detailed recollection.
arguments.strongest_reply: AWARE II itself acknowledges alpha-coma ambiguity and that association does not establish causation; objective participant-level testing remains necessary.
unresolved_issues: Direct post-publication author response not accessed; supplement and detailed participant data unavailable.
